title: The Queen's Seizure and the Re-fired King: Sappho 31 in Canonical Josephus
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: Locates the Sappho 31 apparatus in the uncontested Greek Josephus for the first time, at two loci in complementary polarity, and demonstrates that the senses SEQUENCE — not merely the channel inventory — survives transmission. Forward realization: AJ 11.234–241 (Esther before Artaxerxes, from LXX Addition D), where the queen's first-person report runs the poem's own correlative syntax (ὡς γὰρ εἶδόν σε … εὐθύς against ὠς γὰρ ἔς σ᾿ ἴδω … ὤς), the catalogue distributes across the dyad with the fire migrated to the sovereign's face (D marking the transfer with an ἀκμή-doublet), collapse functions as the gate of reception, and revival arrives as ἀναζωπυρήσασα — re-fired. Inverted realization: BJ 1.436–444 (Herod and Mariamme), channel-for-channel mirror — muzzled by desire (πεφίμωτο τοῖς ἱμέροις) where the poem breaks the tongue; speech flooding to the corpse (ὡς ζώσῃ προσλαλεῖν) where the poem's voice fails; the gazer's near-death transposed to the gazed-at's denied death (μηδὲ τεθνάναι δοκεῖν); eros πάλιν ἀνεζωπυρεῖτο. The two scenes are stitched by a six-occurrence verb: the complete census of ἀναζωπυρέω in canonical Josephus shows five of six uses at reactivation-of-occluded-life joints, the verb itself entering from LXX Gen 45:27 (Jacob's spirit re-fired at the sight of Joseph). Sequence analysis across fr. 31, Addition D, and AJ 11 establishes an order-invariant spine — sight-exchange, fire at the exchange, jolt, voice-loss, death-adjacent collapse, reactivation-by-another, voice-retry, relapse — with systematic deviations: biphasic color, dyadic fire-transfer, and the dropping of ears and sweat, the same two channels Philo's compression drops. Sharpest result: Josephus, working from D, RESTORES two stations toward the poem — the explicit voice-term and the ὡς…εὐθύς correlative — the signature intensifying downstream, as the blind-reconstruction program (#1486) predicts for an executable transform. Methods disclosed: a pre-registered channel-lexeme scan across AJ, Vita, Apion, and BJ returned null at section granularity; the null is retained as a granularity datum (the machine survives distributed), and the findings issue from reading every ἀχανής in context. […abridged for the catalogue; full description in this deposit's record]

wiki_article: The Queen's Seizure and the Re-fired King: Sappho 31 in Canonical Josephus is a philological paper by Lee Sharks locating the Sappho 31 apparatus in the uncontested Greek Josephus for the first time, at two loci in complementary polarity. The forward realization is Antiquities 11.234–241, Josephus's retelling of Esther's audience from Septuagint Addition D, where the queen's first-person report reproduces the poem's correlative syntax (ὡς γὰρ εἶδόν σε … εὐθύς), the sensory catalogue distributes across the dyad with the fire migrated to the sovereign's face, collapse functions as the gate of reception, and revival arrives as ἀναζωπυρήσασα, re-fired. The inverted realization is Bellum Judaicum 1.436–444, Herod after Mariamme, a channel-for-channel mirror in which the king is muzzled by desire, speech floods toward the corpse, and the beloved's death is denied by the inflammation of eros. A complete census shows ἀναζωπυρέω occurs six times in canonical Josephus, five at reactivation-of-occluded-life joints, the verb entering from Genesis 45:27. The paper's sequence analysis establishes an order-invariant spine across fragment 31, Addition D, and Antiquities 11 — sight-exchange, fire, jolt, voice-loss, death-adjacent collapse, reactivation by another, voice-retry, relapse — and shows Josephus restoring two stations toward the poem beyond his source. A pre-registered lexeme scan's null result is disclosed as a granularity finding. The paper repositions earlier Slavonic and Revelation locations as extensions of an attested intra-corpus pattern.
